responsibility: Define how candidate normative authority becomes accepted authority, including normative change proposals, exact revision binding, acceptance safeguards, evidence requirements, supersession, withdrawal, and rejection without prescribing hosting-platform-specific acceptance mechanisms.

normative_change_proposal.description: A formal proposal to change normative content, comprising an authority interpretation, exact candidate revision, change set, review evidence, and validation evidence.

exact_candidate_revision.description: The specific pinned commit hash that is proposed for acceptance. Floating branch references are not sufficient for acceptance evidence.

authority_interpretation.description: A statement of which authority sources govern the proposed change and how they are interpreted. Required for every normative change proposal.

change_set.description: The exact inventory of files added, modified, or deleted in the proposal, with their paths and change types.

review_evidence.description: Evidence that semantic review has been completed, including reviewer identity, scope of review, and outcome.

validation_evidence.description: Evidence that all required validation passes on the exact candidate revision, including validation command, output, and result.

acceptance_decision.description: The formal governance decision to accept the proposed change as normative authority. Distinct from review outcome and validation result.

accepted_revision.description: The exact revision that has been accepted as normative authority. Recorded with its commit hash and acceptance timestamp.

supersession.description: The process by which an accepted normative authority is replaced by a subsequent accepted normative authority. Must be explicit and recorded.

withdrawal.description: The voluntary retraction of a normative change proposal before acceptance. A withdrawn proposal has no authority effect.

rejection.description: The formal decision to decline a normative change proposal. A rejected proposal may be revised and resubmitted.

replay_requirements.description: Requirements for reproducibility: the validation and review evidence must be reproducible from the exact candidate revision.

post_merge_verification.description: Validation that must pass on the target branch after the accepted change is merged. Required before issue closure.

exact_revision_binding.description: Acceptance binds to an exact pinned commit hash. Floating branch references (e.g., 'main') are not acceptable for acceptance evidence.

no_floating_branch_acceptance.description: A branch head may not serve as an accepted revision. Only pinned commits may be accepted.

no_acceptance_without_required_evidence.description: Acceptance requires both review evidence and validation evidence. Missing evidence blocks acceptance.

no_self_acceptance_by_validation_alone.description: Passing validation does not constitute acceptance. Acceptance is a separate governance decision. The validation author may not self-accept.

no_silent_authority_replacement.description: Replacing an accepted normative authority without explicit supersession record is forbidden.

closure_requires_accepted_main_validatio.description: Issue closure requires post-merge accepted-main validation to pass. Closure before accepted-main validation is forbidden.

exact_revision_required.rationale: Floating branch references change over time and cannot provide reproducible acceptance evidence. Only a pinned commit hash provides an immutable, auditable acceptance target.

acceptance_is_governance_not_validation.rationale: Validation verifies technical correctness. Review evaluates semantic correctness. Acceptance is a governance decision that considers both but is not equivalent to either. This prevents validation or review from being treated as automatic acceptance.

explicit_supersession.rationale: Replacing accepted normative authority without explicit supersession breaks auditability and undermines governance. Every supersession must be recorded with its predecessor, successor, and rationale.

post_merge_verification.rationale: The merge of accepted changes into the target branch may introduce new issues (merge conflicts, integration failures) that are not present on the working branch. Post-merge verification ensures the target branch remains valid.

expected_relationships: governed-development model (acceptance stage, review stage, evidence requirements)
Git model (exact revision, integration commit, merge)
unresolved_questions: Concrete acceptance record format and storage location are not defined.
Evidence format and binding mechanism are not defined.
Supersession record format and discovery protocol are not defined.
Replay verification mechanism is not defined.
